analysis.title: USD Rates: Rally First, Narrative Second
key_insights: 10-year Treasury yields are about 35bps below the 5.31% high set at the start of October. Thursday's move was an acceleration of a slow reversal over the prior couple of weeks.

The rally was led by futures (TY and US contracts). Fast Money (FM) shorts being stopped out and covering should continue given proximity to the October FOMC. The desk sees domestic Real Money buying in the belly, but it is small relative to futures activity, which if CTA-led could have legs.

Real Money accounts question the rally's sustainability after a month of firmer CPI/PPI, upside risk to PCE, and a Fed still biased toward tightening even if October is a pass. Breakevens have not rallied meaningfully, and 1y1y CPI looks to be looking through oil.

The author argues the rates reaction function has shifted so that growth and AI capex/financing risks outweigh incremental inflation surprises. The author supports the growth and AI capex concerns but says it is too early and too fast to treat them as fully materializing, and that the framing looks like markets boxing a narrative around the moves.

Given the futures activity and lack of big end-user follow-through, the author sees the move as mostly positioning. CTA/algo/program flows drove this week, and FM short covering drove last week's bursts of duration strength.

The UBS framework needs roughly another 5-10bp of rally before systematic (CTA/risk-parity) demand becomes materially stronger. CTA/risk-parity buying, convexity receiving from options/MBS hedgers and an unwind of leveraged paid-forward positions could reinforce one another. Some knock-on receiving already occurred into Friday morning's options expiry.
Convexity-driven receiving is a reason to be short 30y MMS, which is still rich on Z.

Refunding survey did little to suggest a Bessent twist is imminent, which takes support from 20s. 2027 could see a curve twist effect via reliance on bills and 2/5/7s. Cooperative oil is the other support for WN, but the market has already begun testing the temporary oil relief.

The vol/risk-premia correlation makes the author unwilling to endorse long-end spreads. 30y MMS and forward/levered roll trades are the first to be hit when risk sells off and remain energy sensitive.

Preferred expression is fading the long end in rate: 10x5/15x5 steepeners at about 1.5z look cheap, with about 2.6bp/3m positive roll as a payer. 20s would outpace any 30y move after QRA, and the position is 94% correlated to 10s.

Macro funds gave up on forward dovish expressions and flipped to paid after forward received positions were stopped out violently through the year. 1y1y shorts have moved against holders despite earning 2bps/3m of roll, so forced unwinds could extend the rally even with firm inflation. Positioning may matter more than data at this point in the season.
Europe may offer the better forward, with ERH7/H8 attractive against rising medium-term growth sensitivity.

Oil: crude flows through Hormuz have recovered toward pre-war levels but delivered energy costs have not normalized, because inventories are depleted and rebuilding adds lagged crude demand, transport costs are higher (ship-to-ship transfers, longer routes, insurance, freight), and disruption risk carries a persistent premium. The author sees energy as a stagflationary risk on a vulnerable macro backdrop.

A retracement in duration would not be a surprise given the speed of the move and the temporary nature of CTA program flows. Inflation and term premium can still produce another selloff. Seasonal end of IG supply helps duration.

Hyperscalers are balancing debt with equity raises while paying concessions on debt. Borrowing costs at historically expensive levels add cumulative damage to housing, consumers, leveraged AI infrastructure and corporate credit. The author frames this as a corporate weakness plus growth downturn view, which a 5y5y receiver is designed for.

The author believes the AI theme is shifting from a capex story to a financing/ROIC story, with bullish rates implications. The Street projects hyperscaler/neocloud investment of about $1.6-1.8tn annually in 2027-28, and higher funding costs and tighter credit terms raise cancellation and delay risk. A shift from debt to retained cash, equity and JVs could reduce IG issuance and Treasury rate-lock supply, so rate locks should not be relied on to support long-end spread longs.

The author has a long-standing view that a tech bubble pop could force the Fed to cut in late 2027/2028 and sees merit in Z7 call spreads for premium-defined protection against a financing or growth shock.

geopolitical: Hormuz crude flows have recovered toward pre-war levels, but delivered energy costs have not normalized and a re-escalation is still seen as in the cards.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth and AI capex/financing risks now outweigh inflation surprises in the rates reaction function. Short covering and CTA flows with a large short base, convexity receiving and forced unwinds of paid-forward positions could extend the rally even with firm inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: The author sees the move as mostly positioning, with little end-user follow-through. Firmer CPI/PPI, a Fed biased toward tightening, oil re-escalation risk and term premium could trigger a retracement or another selloff.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CTA demand needs about another 5-10bp of rally to turn materially stronger. A re-test of oil relief or a risk dump would hit long-end spread positions.
